title: AA Batteries 8-pack

adjustment.analysis: No events or price changes in the target week. The baseline already reflects recent trends and seasonality. Past Memorial Day (week before) showed no meaningful lift (noise-adjusted x1.0). Promotions historically lift sales by 21% on average, but no promotion is planned. The recent weekly sales are noisy but within expected variation (CV 34%, ordinary noise 38%). No driver justifies a multiplier shift. The classical uplift model's 1.00 is appropriate.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-38% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
